findings.title: Recurring-cancellation calendar deletes are no longer awaited before Promise.all
findings.body: In the `allRemainingBookings` + `credentialId` branch, calendar deletions are collected by pushing into `apiDeletes` from inside `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`. Because the callback is async and now contains an `await` before the first push, the callback yields immediately and `apiDeletes` is still empty when `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs later in the handler (line 652). The recurring-booking calendar events are therefore never awaited before the request returns, and any rejection from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent` escapes as an unhandled rejection (which terminates Node by default). The sibling branch just below (lines 476-484) was correctly converted to a `for...of` loop with `await`; this branch needs the same conversion.

findings.title: async forEach makes reschedule cancellations fire-and-forget and defeats the try/catch
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` is used inside a `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }`. `forEach` discards the promises returned by the async callback, so the surrounding try/catch can never observe a failure from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`, and those failures become unhandled promise rejections (fatal by default in Node >= 15). `Reschedule` also resolves and returns `true` (and sends the reschedule email) before the external calendar/video events are actually deleted; in a serverless handler the process may be frozen at that point, leaving the old event on the organizer's calendar even though the booking is marked CANCELLED. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop inside the try block.

findings.title: async forEach makes reschedule cancellations fire-and-forget and defeats the try/catch
findings.body: Same defect as in the vital reschedule file: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` returns immediately because `forEach` ignores the promises returned by the async callback. The outer `try/catch` around the loop therefore no longer catches errors from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`, those errors surface as unhandled rejections, and the function resolves before the calendar/video deletions complete, so the old event may remain on the user's calendar after a reschedule. Replace the `forEach` with `await Promise.all(...map(...))` or a `for...of` loop with `await`.

findings.title: requestReschedule deletions are started asynchronously and never awaited
findings.body: The `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` block in the `requestReschedule` mutation discards every returned promise. Before this change the callback was synchronous, so the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls were at least initiated synchronously in the handler; now they are deferred until after the surrounding synchronous code runs (i.e. potentially after `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` and after the mutation returns), and no failure from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` is observed or logged (unhandled rejection, fatal by default in Node). The old calendar/video event for the rescheduled booking can silently survive. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop with `await`.

findings.title: `!calendar` early return skips cleanIntegrationKeys and sends raw credentials to the client
findings.body: In `getConnectedCalendars`, when `getCalendar` returns null the function returns `{ integration, credentialId }` with the raw `integration` object. `integration` comes from `getApps(credentials)`, i.e. the app object that carries `credentials` (including the user's OAuth `key`) and `credential` — see how this same object is used at lines 27-30 of this file. The other two return paths correctly call `cleanIntegrationKeys(integration)` precisely to avoid leaking credentials to the client (there is even a comment "Don't leak credentials to the client"), but this path returns them verbatim, so any credential whose calendar implementation is missing/keyless will ship the user's secrets to the browser via the connectedCalendars endpoint. Pre-existing, but it is inside the function this PR modifies; the return should also be `{ integration: cleanIntegrationKeys(integration), credentialId }`.

findings.title: getCalendar is called for non-calendar-variant apps and its promise is dropped
findings.body: In `getCalendarCredentials`, `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` runs for every credential, but the result is only kept when `app.variant === "calendar"`; for other variants the promise is created and discarded. Now that `getCalendar` is async this is (a) a wasted dynamic `import()` of the app's calendar module for every non-calendar-variant app on every call, and (b) a floating promise whose rejection (e.g. the lazy import failing, or `calendarType.split` on a malformed credential type) becomes an unhandled rejection. Move the `getCalendar` call inside the `app.variant === "calendar"` branch.

findings.title: Commented-out example points at a non-existent path
findings.body: The template comment `// example: import("./example"),` references `./example`, but the example app directory in this package is `_example` (the previous comment was `// import * as example from "./_example";`). A developer copying/uncommenting this template will get a module-resolution error. It should read `// example: import("./_example"),`.
